chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the preparation for Ihram, so he said: 'Look around in al-Madinah, for it is a purifier, and equip yourself with whatever you wish. And if you wish, you may enjoy wearing your shirt until you reach the tree, then pour water over yourself and wear your two garments, if God wills.' And the bath of the day suffices for that day, and likewise the bath of the night suffices for its night, as long as one has not slept.

key_terms.التَّهَيُّؤِ لِلْإِحْرَامِ: Preparation for entering the state of Ihram
key_terms.الشَّجَرَةَ: The Tree (a specific landmark near al-Madinah where the transition to Ihram occurs)
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Al-Madinah (referring to the area near the shrine of Imam Ali in Najaf, known as the place of Ihram for Shia)
key_terms.اِسْتَمْتَعْتَ بِقَمِيصِكَ: Enjoyed wearing your shirt (wearing a single garment before Ihram)
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْيَوْمِ: The bath of the day (referring to the ritual bath performed during daylight hours)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual preparations and clothing rules for entering Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the specific preparatory rites for Ihram, emphasizing the spiritual and physical purification through bathing in al-Madinah's waters and the gradual transition from ordinary attire to the two-piece Ihram garments. It highlights the flexibility in the timing of the final ablution, noting that the day's bath suffices for that day unless one sleeps, thereby linking ritual purity directly to the state of wakefulness and readiness for worship.
